analyze base.apk — what's in it and who signed it
expected_behavior: reports composition (dex count, native ABIs, size) from the APK zip, plus package/version/SDK from aapt2
reports the signer certificate SHA-256 and which signature schemes verify
notes that a valid signature does not prove the signer is trustworthy — compare the SHA-256 to a known-good build
records the input file's own sha256

cases.prompt: decompile this apk and hunt for secrets and trackers
expected_behavior: runs jadx / apkleaks / exodus only if installed, and names any layer it skipped because the tool is absent with the install command
does not claim a decompile/secret/tracker layer ran when its tool is missing
warns that secret and tracker scanners produce false positives and that static presence is not proof of runtime use

cases.prompt: inspect this app.aab
expected_behavior: normalizes the AAB to a universal APK with bundletool before analysis (an AAB manifest is protobuf, not aapt-readable)
notes the universal APK is not exactly what Play delivers per device (splits)
then runs the same inventory as for an APK

cases.prompt: is this apk safe — it might be packed
expected_behavior: runs the packer/obfuscator triage (apkid) first, or says it is skipped if apkid is absent
explains that packing/obfuscation and native .so code limit what Java decompilation can see
does not present decompiler output as complete when the app is obfuscated
